claims.text: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits a large caloric response.
The unmodified alloy has poor structural integrity and is susceptible to cracking during operation.
The intervention is the addition of 2–5 vol% nano-ZrO2 particles.
The nano-ZrO2 composite will be produced by powder metallurgy followed by spark plasma sintering.
Consolidation at approximately 50 MPa and 600–700 °C with a short dwell and minimal post-sintering heat treatment is suitable for this composite.
The 600–700 °C sintering range is below the caloric transformation onset of the alloy.
Processing will produce a homogeneous dispersion of nano-ZrO2 at grain boundaries and within the alloy matrix.
Dispersed ceramic particles will deflect cracks.
Dispersed nano-ZrO2 particles will improve mechanical strength through load transfer.
Nanoscale microstructural reinforcement can increase strength.
The nano-ZrO2 particles will not interfere significantly with the reversible phase transformation responsible for the caloric effect.
Adding nano-ZrO2 will increase compressive or tensile strength by approximately 20–30% relative to the unreinforced alloy.
The entropy-change magnitude will remain within ±5% of that of the unreinforced alloy under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
The proposed strength and caloric-response balance will persist under magnetic fields up to a few tesla.
The proposed performance will persist under equivalent pressure-field operation and typical caloric temperature cycling.
The proposed performance will persist under mechanical loading regimes relevant to structural applications.
Nonuniform nanoparticle dispersion and interfacial reactions could alter transformation kinetics and caloric response.
Failure to achieve the specified 20–30% strength improvement, or a caloric-response deviation exceeding ±5%, will falsify the hypothesis.
